test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In the Climate Change Performance Index 2025, why did India retain a top-10 spot unlike several developed economies?

options.text: High renewable energy share and low per capita emissions

solution:
The correct answer is __**High renewable energy share and low per capita emissions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India retained its top-10 position in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2025 due to its **high share of renewable energy** in the energy mix and **low per capita greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions**.
 
• The country is among the few nations that are **on track to meet their Paris Agreement goals** of limiting global warming to well below 2°C.
 
• India has made significant strides in renewable energy expansion, with **solar and wind energy playing a key role** in reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) emphasize **achieving 50% of its installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources** by 2030.
 
• Unlike many developed nations, India's per capita energy consumption remains low while its renewable energy capacity continues to grow rapidly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI):**

 
 
• The CCPI is an independent monitoring tool that tracks countries' progress in combating climate change.
 
• It assesses nations based on GHG emissions, renewable energy, energy use, and climate policy.
 
• The index is published annually by Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute, and Climate Action Network.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy in India:**
 
 
• India ranks third globally in renewable energy capacity, with over 125 GW of installed capacity (as of 2023).
 
• The country aims to achieve 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.
 
• Major renewable energy sources include solar, wind, hydro, and biomass.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emissions:**
 
 
• India's per capita GHG emissions are approximately 2.4 tons, significantly lower than the global average of 6.3 tons (2022 data).
 
• Efforts to reduce emissions include transitioning to electric mobility, afforestation, and energy efficiency programs.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement Goals:**
 
 
• The 2015 Paris Agreement aims to limit global temperature rise to below 2°C compared to pre-industrial levels.
 
• India has committed to reducing the emission intensity of its GDP by 45% by 2030 from 2005 levels.
 
 
 
• **Challenges for Developed Economies:**
 
 
• Many developed nations struggle to reduce emissions due to high per capita consumption and dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• Transitioning to renewables is slower due to existing infrastructure and policy hurdles.
